# #4477: Patch: the sweep notebook shows pass 2, the pass that bans
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

When the practice AI keeps fumbling a card, an automatic sweep forces that card into its decks and watches what happens. The sweep runs in two passes: a quick screen of every card, then a longer replay of just the suspects, and only the second pass decides whether a card stays banned, goes on a watch list, or is cleared. Today the analysis notebook draws only the first pass, so anyone reviewing a sweep sees the smoke but not the verdict: a card the screen flagged but the replay cleared still looks guilty. After this change the notebook gains one more table with the replay numbers per suspect card — its games, affordable turns, plays, average effect on the AI's evaluation, and whether it was banned, watched, or cleared.

## Why

- The ban logic reads the second pass, not the first. In `crates/ai/src/sweep.rs`, `at_risk_ids` puts a card on the suspect list from half-strength pass-1 flags, while `sweep_verdict` bans only from pass-2 totals: `neverPlayed` needs `second.playable_turns >= AI_SWEEP.ban_affordable_turns` (6) with zero plays, `selfHarm` needs `second.eval_delta_count >= AI_SWEEP.ban_harm_plays` (8), `selfKill` needs `second.losing_plays >= AI_SWEEP.ban_losing_plays` (4). Pass-1 games run 8 per card and tier; pass-2 runs 24 per at-risk card (`sweep2:<tier>:<id>:<n>` seeds).
- The analysis drops exactly that pass: `load_sweep` in `analysis/jackioh_records/__init__.py` skips every line naming a `forced` card without a `defId`, and `analysis/README.md` plus notebook 03's own intro describe the notebook as pass 1 only.
- Every sweep of record ends as a shadow-ban pull request (SPEC §9.9, R186/R390), yet the review tool cannot answer the review question. The repo's own sweep test comment gives the concrete case: meditative-022 was at risk, pass 2 cleared its deal but not its watch (`crates/tools/src/sweep.rs`, fixture test) — the notebook can show neither half of that outcome today.

## Proposal

- Add a second loader, e.g. `load_sweep_pass2`, returning one row per at-risk card and tier from the skipped lines: games, affordable and playable turns, plays, eval-delta mean and count, losing plays, and the half/full flag reading behind them.
- Add a "Pass 2: the verdicts" section to `analysis/notebooks/03-ai-sweep-and-generations.ipynb` rendering that frame, including the cleared-but-watched middle outcome, and saying so when a sweep file holds no pass-2 lines.
- Extend `analysis/fixtures/sweep-small.jsonl` with a few pass-2 lines (the fixture remake command in `analysis/README.md` already plays them) and cover the loader and the new cells in `analysis/tests/test_load.py` and `analysis/tests/test_notebooks.py`, following the existing `flagged_sweep` pattern.

## Where it lands

- `analysis/jackioh_records/__init__.py` (new loader beside `load_sweep`), `analysis/notebooks/03-ai-sweep-and-generations.ipynb`, `analysis/fixtures/sweep-small.jsonl`, `analysis/tests/test_load.py`, `analysis/tests/test_notebooks.py`.
- SPEC sections: §9.9 (R186, R390); no new ruling and no spec-text change — it only surfaces numbers the sweep already writes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `load_sweep` output is unchanged on files with and without pass-2 lines.
- [ ] The new loader reads a whole sweep's files named together, one row per at-risk card and tier, and refuses a duplicate card-and-tier and a non-result line naming file and line, as `load_sweep` does.
- [ ] Notebook 03 shows the pass-2 table on the extended fixture, prints the cleared and cleared-but-watched states distinctly from bans, and still runs on an empty sweep and on a pass-1-only file.
- [ ] `uv run --project analysis pytest analysis/tests` passes and the notebook is committed without outputs.

## Size and risks

Small: Python and notebook only, no engine, card, AI, or gate behavior changes, so no floor or threshold the owner must approve. Main risk is drift between the pass-2 JSON shape and the loader, held by the loader tests; the fixture is remade only via the documented sweep command, never by hand.
